column1: # Probe benchmark cases for scripts/bench-probes (docs/infrastructure/cloud-benchmarks.md; why each: perf/bench/targets.md).

# kind: only = --only the target items (comma list) | cert = --only over today's write-elf certificate of SYMBOL, its items matching GLOB (target SYMBOL:GLOB) | warm = check after a priming run | elf-warm / elf-cold = write-elf the target symbol

column6: why
fixed cost of loading the native world warm: every native process pays it
a fully warm write-elf of the smallest tool (the PR lane's native smoke): no kernel work left
the smoke cold, as on a fresh box: certificate kernel-checked from scratch
a mid-sized tool cold: certificate kernel work grows with the code
the heaviest native tool test (a heap tool: arena, procedures, a sort loop), cold
the second heaviest, cold: the heap tools' shared cost shows where the two agree
piece_N_is: the assembler evaluated by the kernel, one per code piece; the largest certificate family
at_N: the label prefixes of the program, gated as Prog literals; the second certificate family
the heaviest kernel item of lib/native alone: a lemma at a neutral Target that runs millions of steps
the second: one kernel check of millions of steps
a small kernel-and-omega item of the same module, the fast inner-loop case
the heaviest declaration of the cold library (2026-11-11): a compiler-correctness lemma over a call's whole sequence, and the library's peak memory
the heaviest x86 machine item: omega over stack layouts
one of the heaviest declarations of the cold library (2026-11-11): the points a Cauchy sequence stays above are located: linarith and the half lemmas over an ordered field's carrier
one of the heaviest declarations of the cold library (2026-11-11): the converse of IsTrace::bind, a dependent match over the tree and the trace's three shapes
a runtime fn linking two dozen callees: the generator and the linking proof, which must follow the count of callees and not their code

the heaviest declaration of the cold library (2026-11-16): a `simp_only` whose goal's sides are a record a 64-pass loop computes; the value machine has it at once and the substitution reducer respells it, five times (issues/small-step-reducer-on-computed-terms.md)

the smallest case of the same, a copy of `clamp_literal` (lib/_tests/std/tactic/simp_branch_tests.hthr): `clamp(70, 10, 50) = 50` by `simp_only(clamp)`, two comparisons of u64 literals done by substitution

a `runtime fn` loop over an array with three found index proofs, a copy of `Sched::expand` (lib/_tests/native/runtime/runtime_held_index_tests.hthr): omega's reflection, whose reduce-and-name step is the same reducer, run at each copy of the body
the same search with nothing lifted, a copy of `block_spread` (lib/_tests/std/core/squash_conditions_tests.hthr): what one `bv_omega` index goal costs per copy of a `decreases` body
the heaviest kernel item of the cold library (2026-11-16) and its peak memory: one long proof under fifteen binders, substitution in the elaborator and the gate both

one of the heaviest declarations of the cold library (2026-11-18): linarith and ring inside a plain match's arms, where 5,400 checking fallbacks each ask whether the match's test occurs in both types (issues/match-arm-coercion-abstracts-both-types.md)

a chain of nested eq_dec arms building ByteDecode(bytes): 62,000 lookups of the type-code template instance table, each a deep comparison of equal but unshared arguments, are most of its syntax-equality nodes (issues/template-instance-table-deep-compare.md)

a six-line runtime fn whose generator publishes thousands of declarations: its time is the generator running on the kernel's evaluator through the host and reading its reply one field at a time (issues/runtime-generator-link-cost.md)
a refl over binary64 exp: the kernel gate's slowest item per evaluator step in the 2026-11-18 cold library (about 7 µs a step against a median of 0.5), its steps over large rationals
